Looks like an average home tinkerer mig welder.

I wouldn't try & weld anything thicker than 1/8" (bevel prep above 16 ga). You can either use cored wire & experience frustration or go with solid wire & shielding gas for a more enjoyable experience.

Stick with 100% CO2 if you go that route because you'll have trouble getting a decent weld profile with a higher quality gas. The machine simply doesn't have the necessary output to compensate for an argon mix. If you're lucky a 75-25 argon/CO2 mix might work with .025" wire... but that's for sheet metal really & not worth the expense imo.

Preheating will be your best bet on any job involving anything between 16ga & 1/8th.
So this machine is just for welding thin metals?

Well... there's always a way. But I wouldn't weld anything thick if someone's life were to depend on it.

With proper preheating & multiple passes you could go 3/16" or even 1/4" but that's pushing it. Would probably fry the machine doing long welds since it only has a 20% duty cycle... 2 minutes of welding for 8 minutes of cool down is what this means.
